properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: hash.js@1.1.3 implements the SHA-1/SHA-2 family; declared in the v2 lockfile (v3's lockfile resolves it too). Transitive dep of elliptic@6.5.4 (ethers' @ethersproject/signing-key secp256k1 signing), @ethersproject/sha2/@ethersproject/pbkdf2, and ethereum-cryptography@0.1.3. Toolchain hashing surface; no application call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: secp256k1 ECDSA curve packages declared in both projects' npm lockfiles. All 16 sites are lockfile entries — @noble/secp256k1@1.6.3 (via @scure/bip32@1.1.0, BIP-32 HD-wallet lib in hardhat's toolchain) and secp256k1@4.0.1 + @types/secp256k1@4.0.1 (via ethereum-cryptography@0.1.3 ← ethereumjs-util ← @metamask/eth-sig-util). This is also the LIVE curve: ethers ^5.7.1 signs every deployment transaction with ECDSA-secp256k1 (see the two ECDSA-secp256k1 findings at scripts/deplo

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Transitive dependency in the hardhat toolchain; no first-party call site. Symmetric password KDF — Grover square-root only, not Shor-vulnerable.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: evp_bytestokey@1.0.3 — OpenSSL's legacy single-round MD5-based EVP_BytesToKey KDF, declared in both lockfiles (version pin + package block in each). Transitive via browserify-aes@1.2.0 ← ethereum-cryptography@0.1.3 in the hardhat/ethers build toolchain. The KDF ships with the build; no call site in the application code (the app is 4 Solidity contracts + hardhat deploy scripts).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: tweetnacl@0.14.5 provides Ed25519 signatures. Pulled into the toolchain by sshpk@1.17.0 (~0.14.0 — OpenSSH key handling in the request/http-signature chain) and bcrypt-pbkdf@1.0.2 (^0.14.3); @metamask/eth-sig-util@4.0.1 separately pulls tweetnacl@1.0.3. No Ed25519 use in the application code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The application's only exercised cryptographic primitive: every deployment/transaction signature. secp256k1 is fixed by the Ethereum protocol, so the eventual ML-DSA-65 migration is a chain-protocol decision, not app-changeable.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Library API surface shipped in the build via the ethers v5 signing stack; key-agreement capability would be retroactively breakable under Shor if ever exercised — it is not exercised here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: tweetnacl@0.14.5 also provides X25519 key agreement (scalar multiplication). Same package declarations and provenance as the Ed25519 object (sshpk, bcrypt-pbkdf); distinct primitive — kept as its own entry. No application call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: Keccak-256 hash implementations shipped in the build (both lockfiles) for the ethers/hardhat toolchain; used indirectly by every transaction and address.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: PBKDF2 implementations shipped for the ethers v5 keystore format (password → keystore encryption key); not exercised by this app, which signs with a raw env private key.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: scrypt KDF implementations shipped for ethers keystore JSON encryption; not exercised by this app.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: SHA-256 provided by @noble/hashes@1.1.2, declared in the v2 lockfile (v3 mirrors). @noble/hashes is required by @scure/bip32@1.1.0/@scure/bip39@1.1.0 (BIP-32/39 HD-wallet derivation in hardhat's toolchain) and @noble/secp256k1@1.6.3 (RFC-6979 ECDSA/ECDH on secp256k1 uses SHA-256 internally). No application call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Hash algorithm available in the shipped @noble/hashes library (via @scure/bip32/bip39); quantum-acceptable (Grover square-root only), no app call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Second SHA-3 provider in the build (noble), alongside the keccak/ethers stack; quantum-acceptable, no app call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: tweetnacl@0.14.5's secretbox authenticated encryption (XSalsa20 stream cipher + Poly1305 MAC). Same package declarations and provenance as the Ed25519/X25519 objects (sshpk@1.17.0, bcrypt-pbkdf@1.0.2); @metamask/eth-sig-util's encrypt path uses the tweetnacl line too. Distinct primitive (ae) — own entry. No application call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: the tweetnacl crypto library ships at two versions in the toolchain — 0.14.5 (required by sshpk@1.17.0 for OpenSSH key handling and bcrypt-pbkdf@1.0.2) and 1.0.3 + tweetnacl-util@0.15.1 (required by @metamask/eth-sig-util@4.0.1) — across both projects' lockfiles. Provider behind the Ed25519 (ALG-683d5cd2), X25519 (ALG-defedad1) and XSalsa20-Poly1305 (ALG-f58a8f00) objects. Toolchain-only; no application call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @noble/hashes@1.1.2, required by @scure/bip32@1.1.0 and @scure/bip39@1.1.0 (BIP-32/39 HD-wallet derivation shipped with hardhat's toolchain) and by @noble/secp256k1's users. Provides SHA-256/SHA-512/keccak/ripemd/blake2 — provider behind the SHA-256 object ALG-928ac765. No application call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt KDF implementation shipped with the ethers v4 copy inside hardhat-etherscan's verification toolchain; dependency inventory entry, not exercised by the app.
